subject: Scope & exception for ephemeral logs — post-demo recap
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@medinova.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Scope & exception for ephemeral logs — post-demo recap

Hi Alex / Sasha,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to see the Medinova team’s use case. Per our demo, I wanted to capture the open data-handling items and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of asks from your side:
- 0-retention for full conversational transcripts (no persistent storage of user prompts / responses)
- KV prefix/cache retention limited to 24 hours for short-lived context features
- EU region residency for all inference-serving and logs (primary region: eu-west-1)
- Audit evidence: SOC 2 report + access to retention configuration logs during procurement

Redwood constraints and options (what we can offer):
- 0-retention: we can provide an opt-in policy that disables transcript persistence for your tenant; caveat: short-lived KV (1–24h) is required to support multi-turn sessions and retrieval — we can limit that to 1 day and encrypt keys with your KMS.
- Short logs window: for request/response auditability (errors, throttles) we keep minimal metadata (no content) for 7 days by default; we can negotiate down to 3 days for a pilot in EU region.
- Data residency: we can pin inference + logs to EU regions and exclude cross-region backups.
- Evidence: attaching our standard security questionnaire and a draft redline of the data terms for your legal team.

Proposed next steps and timeline:
1) You to complete the attached Medinova Security Questionnaire and highlight any must-haves (Alex) — target by Nov 19.
2) Redwood to prepare a pilot config: 0-retention transcripts + KV TTL = 24h, logs minimal metadata 3 days in eu-west-1. We'll include KMS integration notes (Priya / Karthik) — delivery by Nov 18.
3) Legal review of the redline (both sides) + DocuSign path if acceptable — aim to start procurement week of Nov 22.

If any of the caveats above are deal-breakers (e.g., absolutely zero KV retention), flag them now and we’ll loop in product/infra to evaluate risk.

Attachments: Medinova_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (security form), redlines_data_terms.xlsx (first pass redline).

Thanks,

Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

Thanks Priya — useful recap. A few clarifying Qs before we fill out the questionnaire: 

1) When you say KV TTL = 24h, is that a hard limit on the platform or a recommendation? Can we configure it per-route?
2) For the 0-retention mode, what exactly is disabled? Is there any content kept transiently for debugging (e.g., crash dumps) and if so how long?
3) Can you confirm that token-level billing and usage reporting will not expose PII in the reports provided to our product team?

Procurement timeline: our legal/security team wants the completed questionnaire by Nov 20; procurement kickoff expected Nov 23 if items are OK. We may ask for a short trial (2-week pilot) behind a VPN.

I attached our internal security questionnaire (short form) — please add Redwood responses inline if possible.

Appreciate it,
Alex

--
Alex Moreno
Director of ML Platforms, Medinova
alex@medinova.com
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@medinova.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sasha Ivanov <sasha@medinova.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Scope & exception for ephemeral logs — post-demo recap

Alex — answering inline below (I've also annotated the attached PDF and included a draft config):

> 1) When you say KV TTL = 24h, is that a hard limit on the platform or a recommendation? Can we configure it per-route?

Our platform allows per-tenant and per-route TTLs. For the pilot we propose setting the route used by your clinical assistant to 24h. We can lower to 1h on other routes. TTLs are enforced by the runtime — we do not persist KV beyond its TTL. This is configurable via the Redwood Console or via API (we'll provide the CLI snippet).

> 2) For the 0-retention mode, what exactly is disabled? Is there any content kept transiently for debugging (e.g., crash dumps) and if so how long?

0-retention disables transcript persistence and prevents write-to-disk of conversational content. For operational safety we do retain ephemeral crash traces in-memory and redact any captured content; those traces are discarded within 48 hours and are only accessible to SREs via a restricted audit workflow. If you need a stricter SLA we can design a canary that disables crash capture entirely for your tenant, but there is a higher operational risk (slower root cause analysis).

> 3) Can you confirm that token-level billing and usage reporting will not expose PII in the reports provided to our product team?

Yes — our billing/usage exports contain token counts, latency percentiles, and anonymized route identifiers. We do not include raw content or PII. If you want, we can sign a data handling addendum that explicitly states billing exports exclude content.

Pilot config attached: 
- transcripts.persist: false
- kv.ttl_seconds: 86400
- logs.metadata_window_days: 3 (eu-west-1)
- kms_key: customer-managed (option to provide)

Next steps (updated):
- Priya to share pilot config and CLI example by EOD Nov 17 (done — attached).
- Medinova to return questionnaire with any must-haves highlighted by Nov 19 (Alex).
- Internal review with infra/product for canary option if you request zero crash traces (Karthik to advise).

Attaching: Redwood_pilot_config.yml (stub), annotated_security_questionnaire.pdf (inline answers).

Thanks — I’ll loop Karthik on the canary question.

PRIYA
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Alex Moreno <alex@medinova.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Scope & exception for ephemeral logs — post-demo recap

Alex / Priya — quick internal note:

We can approve the pilot as proposed: 0-retention transcripts + KV TTL = 24h + logs metadata 3 days in eu-west-1.
Caveats:
- We need Medinova to accept an operational SLA that allows SRE access to redacted in-memory crash traces for up to 48h to diagnose production incidents. If they want that disabled entirely, we’ll require an escalation playbook and longer RTO commitments.
- For the production rollout, recommend a canary (10% traffic) in eu-west-1 for 2 weeks to validate behavior and autoscaling under the reduced logging surface.

Priya: I’ll prepare the canary runbook and the short A/B rollback policy. Alex: happy to join a quick call if Medinova’s security needs to talk through the crash-trace tradeoffs.

Karthik
VP, Product — Redwood Inference
